e phenotype of BSCL is typical (acromegaloid facies, muscle hypertrophy, acanthosis nigricans, decreased body fat, mild enophthalmos, among others), the clinical diagnosis of BSCL is relatively easy but requires a clinical suspicion (Fig. 1). Quite often, parents report that since birth or early in life the child had a different appearance, however, diagnosis is usually delayed. Acanthosis nigricans, acromegaloid facies, prognathism, atrophic cheeks (loss of Bichat’s fat ball), abdominal distension with protruding navel, phlebomegaly, and muscle hypertrophy are other common clinical findings (Fig. 1).
